title: Change Fee by Journey Origin and Itinerary Class
content:
**Fare rule clause — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** The change fee is the fare brand's United States-origin change fee when the ticket's journey originates in the United States; when the journey originates outside the United States it is the fare brand's short-haul change fee for domestic and short-haul international itineraries and its long-haul change fee for long-haul international itineraries. The fee is stated to the cent.

## Selection table

| Region where the journey originates | Itinerary class of the ticket | Fee used |
|---|---|---|
| United States | Any | The fare brand's United States-origin change fee |
| Outside the United States | Domestic | The fare brand's short-haul change fee (outside-US origin) |
| Outside the United States | Short-haul international | The fare brand's short-haul change fee (outside-US origin) |
| Outside the United States | Long-haul international | The fare brand's long-haul change fee (outside-US origin) |

The origin region and itinerary class are those recorded on the ticket; the three fees are those of the ticket's fare brand in its exchange terms. The fee concerns the latest voluntary, standard exchange recorded on the ticket.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

Suppose a fare brand's change fees were 0 dollars for United States-origin journeys, 110 dollars short-haul and 260 dollars long-haul for journeys originating outside the United States. A long-haul international ticket whose journey originates outside the United States would carry a change fee of 260.00 dollars; a domestic ticket originating in the United States, 0.00 dollars.
